predecessors.name: Qin dynasty
predecessors.text: the Qin commanderies of Nanhai, Guilin and Xiang in Lingnan, founded 214 BC and run by Zhao Tuo; Cliopatria's shape without Âu Lạc's land

successors.name: Han dynasty
successors.text: 'divided into the seven commanderies of Nanhai, Cangwu, Yulin, Hepu, Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, and Rinan' (Nanyue page), with Hainan inside the page's extent

ledger.x: 204: Zhao Tuo founds the Kingdom of Nanyue at Panyu.
196: Zhao Tuo submits to the Han.
183: Zhao Tuo breaks with the Han.
183: the Yi tribes of Yelang declare allegiance.
179: Nanyue submits to the Han again.
135: Minyue attacks and is no longer a subject.
112: Lü Jia's coup ends Nanyue's submission.
111: Yelang's allegiance to Nanyue ends with Nanyue ('until Nanyue's demise in 111 BC').
111: the Kingdom of Nanyue ends after 93 years ('ending Nanyue's 93-year existence'); the last king Zhao Jiande fled Panyu by boat.

wars.name: First Han-Nanyue antagonism (the Changsha war)
wars.outcome: Nanyue, embargoed by Empress Lü's officials, declared its king emperor, attacked Changsha and defeated the Han's first attack; in 179 Zhao Tuo withdrew the imperial title and returned to nominal submission.

wars.name: Minyue's invasion of Nanyue
wars.outcome: Minyue attacked the border towns; Zhao Mo appealed to the Han, which sent Wang Hui and Han Anguo to attack Minyue from two directions.

wars.name: Han conquest of Nanyue
wars.outcome: Lü Jia killed the pro-Han king and the Han emissaries in 112; Emperor Wu sent 100,000 men in autumn 111; Panyu fell that winter, Zhao Jiande and Lü Jia fled by boat, and Nanyue became seven Han commanderies.

certainty.note: Nanyue's lands are given as modern provinces and commanderies, never as a surveyed line; the Minyue and Yelang parts are subject or loosely allied lands whose frontier is softer still.
